newsitem.title: USA: IMF makes extra funds available to Philippines.
newsitem.headline: IMF makes extra funds available to Philippines.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Friday it would extend an existing $652 million loan to the Philippines to the end of the year and supplement it with an additional $435 million to back 1997 policies.

An IMF statement said $699 million would be available to Manila immediately and the remaining would be made available after a review of economic performance at the end of September. The Philippines authorities promised to back the IMF program with strong fiscal and monetary policies.
The Philippines had asked for IMF help after it was forced to let the peso float following strong speculative pressure.

The extra funding would give the country time to allow a tax reform package to pass through parliament and provide extra resources to support the currency float and discourage speculative capital flows.

The IMF said the Philippines would keep interest rates high until the foreign exchange market has stabilized. Base money growth would be reduced to a level consistent with targets for growth and inflation and fiscal policy would be tightened in the second half to offset slippages in the first half, both by boosting revenue and by cutting spending.
The IMF forecast GDP growth of 6.3 percent this year and inflation of 6.5 percent. The economy grew 5.7 percent last year, while consumer price inflation was 8.4 percent.
